section_summary: This section contains the conclusion of one copy and two further copies of Kilsoo K. Haan’s polemical article “Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii,” together with letters transmitting it to State Department officials and congressional committees in July 1939. The article alleges that Japanese diplomatic, educational, religious, and citizenship practices obstructed the Americanization of Japanese Hawaiians and created a strategic danger to Hawaii. It places those claims within a broader warning about Japanese expansion in Asia and the Pacific, advocates an embargo on war materials and moral support for China and Korea, and compares the situations of Hawaii and Guam with Korea’s loss of independence.

subfiles.title: Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii (concluding pages of an earlier copy)
subfiles.about: The concluding portion argues that Japanese institutions in Hawaii fostered loyalty to Japan and that Japanese expansion endangered American security in Asia and the Pacific.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages discuss alleged restoration of Japanese nationality, dual citizenship, Japanese-language schools, and religious and cultural institutions in Hawaii. The author connects these claims to Japanese fortification and expansion in Manchuria, China, Korea, and the Pacific islands. He concludes by urging an American embargo on war materials and moral assistance to China and Korea.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting “Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii” to Edward Yardley
subfiles.from: Kilsoo K. Haan, Sino-Korean Peoples League
subfiles.to: Edward Yardley, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Haan forwards his article and requests attention to Japanese activities in the Pacific and Western Hemisphere.
subfiles.summary: Haan sends Yardley 'Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii', presented to Senate committees, saying Korean and Chinese warnings were vindicated and urging a positive American policy.

subfiles.title: Submission letter to Senate committees concerning Hawaii and Guam
subfiles.from: Sino-Korean Peoples League of Hawaii, signed by Kilsoo K. Haan
subfiles.to: Members of the Senate Foreign Relations, Naval, and Military Committees, Seventy-Sixth Congress
subfiles.about: The League submits Haan’s article and compares the strategic vulnerability of Guam and Hawaii with Korea’s former position before Japanese annexation.
subfiles.summary: Letter to Senate committees cites Laura Thompson's report that Guam's inhabitants feared Japanese domination and wanted fortification; compares appeasement to Munich. Pages 437-438 duplicate.

subfiles.title: Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii (complete enclosure)
subfiles.to: Members of the Senate Foreign Relations, Naval, and Military Committees
subfiles.about: Haan presents an extended warning that Japanese influence among Hawaii’s population and Japan’s wider Pacific strategy threatened the islands and American security.
subfiles.summary: The article surveys Japanese expansion across East Asia and the Pacific, historical Japanese diplomatic pressure on Hawaii, racial tensions, the Prince Fushimi Scholarship Fund, religious organizations, dual nationality, and Japanese-language schools. It alleges coordinated efforts by Japanese officials and community institutions to preserve Japanese loyalty among Hawaii-born citizens and to prepare a strategic base for future conflict. The conclusion links Hawaii’s defense to events in China and Korea and recommends an embargo on war supplies to Japan and moral aid for Chinese and Korean resistance. Several internal pages appear twice in the file.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting “Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii” to Cordell Hull
subfiles.from: Kilsoo K. Haan, Sino-Korean Peoples League
subfiles.about: Haan sends Secretary Hull a copy of his article and urges an active American response to Japanese policy in the Pacific.
subfiles.summary: Haan sends Hull the article presented to Senate committees, describing Japanese aggression as penetration of the Western sphere and appealing for a more positive American policy.

subfiles.title: Submission letter to Senate committees concerning Hawaii and Guam (copy)
subfiles.from: Sino-Korean Peoples League of Hawaii, signed by Kilsoo K. Haan
subfiles.to: Members of the Senate Foreign Relations, Naval, and Military Committees, Seventy-Sixth Congress
subfiles.about: This copy submits the article and urges protection of Guam and Hawaii against the fate suffered by Korea.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the League's letter citing Laura Thompson's report of Guamanian fear of Japanese rule and comparing Guam and Hawaii with Korea.

subfiles.title: Japanization, A Peril to Hawaii (third copy, incomplete in this section)
subfiles.about: A further enclosure begins Haan’s article and repeats its warning about Japanese political, military, educational, and cultural influence in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: The available pages contain the preface, contents, discussion of Japan’s asserted national mission and Pacific strategy, and accounts of Japanese diplomatic pressure on nineteenth-century Hawaii. They continue with “duck diplomacy,” racial tensions, the Prince Fushimi Scholarship Fund, Japanese Christianity, and the beginning of the section on expatriation. The copy continues beyond page 463, and several pages within this portion are duplicated.
